exposure: Preeclampsia status (compared to normotensive status) in women receiving regional anaesthesia (subarachnoid blockade) for caesarean section
outcome: Hemodynamic effects (hypotension, bradycardia, hemodynamic stability, vasopressor requirements)
cohort: The study included 100 normotensive ASA grade II parturients and 100 ASA grade III preeclamptic parturients, all planned for LSCS.
finding: Subarachnoid blockade is associated with better perioperative hemodynamic stability and lower risk of hypotension and vasopressor requirements in preeclamptic women compared to healthy subjects.
mod_finding: The study concluded that subarachnoid blockade during caesarean section offers better perioperative hemodynamic stability and lower risk of hypotension and vasopressor requirements for preeclamptic women compared to healthy subjects.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken at the time of caesarean section, with data collected from March 2019 to February 2020.
gest_age: Approximately 39 weeks (39.14 +/- 0.54 weeks in preeclamptic and 39.07 +/- 0.77 weeks in normotensive women)
